piece.caption:
How Indian small businesses build AI literacy across their entire workforce.

Data from the joint Zoho and LinkedIn report shows that Indian SMBs with in-house AI talent grew their headcount 5.2 percentage points faster in early 2026. However, while 16.3 percent of firms have AI engineering skills, only 6.1 percent have built everyday AI literacy across regular employees. You do not need custom software to scale. Start by training non-technical staff to use AI search, draft customer follow-ups, and answer standard HR queries behind secure Bring-Your-Own-Key guardrails. Set up these basic systems before your team reaches 50 people.

Which simple workflow in your office takes up the most staff time each week?

hook: Why AI literate small business teams hire 5.2% faster
material:
[83] YourStory — Zoho–LinkedIn report: AI is helping Indian SMBs grow, but skills lag behind
URL: https://yourstory.com/2026/11/indian-smbs-ai-talent-headcount-growth-zoho-linkedin-report
Zoho–LinkedIn report: AI is helping Indian SMBs grow, but skills lag behind | YourStory Sidebar is Loading... ADVERTISEMENT Picture a typical Indian small-business founder. They run sales, approve leave requests and chase late payments. Their contacts are the company's biggest asset, and their WhatsApp is where most deals get done.
That model builds plenty of businesses, but it also caps how big they can get. The New Rules of Growth: How India's SMBs Are Building to Scale , a new joint report from Zoho and LinkedIn , looks at what happens when that cap arrives. Its answer: growing SMBs are moving work out of the founder's head and into systems, skills and teams.
The study covers July 2024 to June 2026. It combines LinkedIn network data from more than 1.4 billion members, including over 193 million in India, with usage data from more than 78,000 organisations on Zoho Workplace , Zoho People and Bigin by Zoho CRM . It defines an SMB as an India-headquartered business with 11 to 200 employees. The stakes are high: according to the Economic Survey 2025-26 , SMBs contribute about 31% of India's GDP and nearly 49% of its exports.
Rather than shrinking their workforce, SMBs that invest in AI talent are hiring faster. In the first half of 2026, Indian SMBs with in-house AI talent grew headcount 5.2 percentage points faster than other SMBs. That is more than double the 2.1-point gap among SMBs globally.
The lift isn't limited to software. Technology leads at 8.9 points, but construction (7.7), wholesale (7.3) and financial services (6.9) are close behind. The link is also strongest in smaller firms: among mid-market companies, the gap shrinks to 0.9 points.
"Those investing in AI talent are showing that AI and jobs can grow together," said Kumaresh Pattabiraman, India Country Manager at LinkedIn . The report adds a caveat: the data shows associations, not cause and effect.
The headline number has a weak spot. SMBs are better at building AI than at using it. LinkedIn data shows 16.3% have AI engineering skills in-house, but only 6.1% have everyday AI literacy across their workforce. Among large enterprises, the figures are more than 34% and 18%.
For most small businesses, everyday literacy matters more. A retailer or manufacturer doesn't need to build AI, but its people need to know how to use it. Pattabiraman's next step: make AI "a skill for every employee, not a specialist skill for a few."
Part of the reason for the slow rollout is caution. AI-assisted search on Zoho Workplace has roughly doubled, and early adopters are using Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) setups. These connect an AI model of the firm's choice using its own access key, so AI use stays within the contracts and data policies it already manages.
SMBs want the productivity of generative AI, but they are wary of sending sensitive data to outside providers. Use of password management tools has also risen about 35%.
Size matters too. Only 8.6% of micro-firms on Zoho People use AI in their HR tools, compared with 29.6% of larger SMBs. "Despite all the attention on AI, adoption still follows operational maturity," said Praval Singh, VP of Marketing and CX at Zoho .
More than 80,000 India-headquartered SMB founders on LinkedIn average over 1,300 connections each. Yet only about one in three SMBs has a formal sales leader at Director, VP or CXO level. In most firms, the founder is both head of sales and the face of the brand.
AI is helping lean teams go further. In the 12 months to June 2026, SMB sellers who used AI did roughly 40% more sales activity than those who didn't, and reached nearly twice as many decision-makers. They also grew their networks faster: in the year after adopting AI, their monthly new connections rose 40%, against 31% for similar sellers who didn't.
Meanwhile, routine sales work is moving into software, from the first chat to the final payment. Bigin by Zoho CRM data shows:
Workflow automation rose about 42% , routing new leads and flagging stalled deals automatically.
Payment link usage grew about 56% , helping customers pay as soon as a deal is agreed.
WhatsApp messages sent through the CRM rose almost sixfold , as deals move to mobile and to the channels buyers already use.
Buyers now size up a business long before they talk to it, and more SMBs are making sure they can be found.
Monthly active SMB advertisers on LinkedIn grew about 13% year on year, and click-through rates rose roughly 81%. The most engaging 10% of advertisers keep campaigns running 26% longer and use 83% more ad creatives than the bottom 10%. About one in six SMB advertisers now mention AI in their ads, mostly as "AI-powered" or "AI-driven" rather than "AI-native."
In HR, the tipping point comes at about 50 employees. Below it, attendance lives on a spreadsheet and leave is approved in a WhatsApp group. Beyond it, informal processes start to fail. Among Zoho People customers, 68% of larger SMBs use several advanced HR features, against just 9% of micro-firms. About 16% of SMBs on the platform use its AI assistant to handle routine HR queries.
Founders want tools that fit how they already work. Custom workflows (about 35%) and custom modules (27%) are the most used advanced features, well ahead of ready-made ones such as performance management (14%).
Skills-based hiring widens the search. Employers in India that hire for skills rather than job titles or degrees can reach 11 times more candidates, and 22 times more for AI roles.
SMBs are also hiring across borders. Their share of hires made outside India rose from about 22% to nearly 27% between 2025 and 2026, led by the US, UAE, UK and Nigeria.
The report doesn't describe a sweeping transformation. It describes steady, practical progress. Indian SMBs are adopting technology one function at a time and building systems around the people who already make the business work. For founders, the lessons are clear:
Start with one workflow , such as sales follow-ups or routine HR questions.
Put guardrails in place first , within your existing permissions and data policies.
Build systems before you reach 50 employees , not after things start to break.
Teach AI to everyone , not just a few specialists.
As Singh put it, the priority is "building the skills to use it well, so they can scale without losing agility." The founder's network still opens the first doors. What this report shows is what it takes to keep growing after that.
